detail:
NIDDK describes its Division of Kidney, Urologic, and Hematologic Diseases as providing funding and support for basic, translational, and clinical research on the kidney and urinary tract. Within kidney research, the division lists chronic kidney disease among its areas, alongside diabetic kidney disease, polycystic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, kidney repair and regeneration, and normal and abnormal kidney development and physiology.

Related NIDDK health information describes the directions this research takes in CKD specifically: long-running cohort studies examining risk factors for progression and the link between CKD and cardiovascular disease, and the Kidney Precision Medicine Project, which studies human kidney tissue to build an atlas of kidney anatomy and explore novel therapies. Sources present these efforts as ongoing work to understand progression and improve future prevention and treatment, not as established therapies.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about chronic kidney disease research and clinical trials.
sourceName: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
summary: NIDDK outlines its kidney research portfolio, spanning basic, translational, and clinical studies of chronic kidney disease, including cohort studies of progression and cardiovascular links and a precision medicine project studying human kidney tissue.
takeaways: NIDDK funds basic, translational, and clinical kidney research through its KUH division
cohort studies examine risk factors for CKD progression and cardiovascular links
precision medicine work studies kidney tissue to explore future therapies
title: Chronic Kidney Disease: precision medicine and progression research
